data.narrative:
Natilus is a Series A autonomous systems company in the drones and autonomous sector. The target has raised $16M to date. The broader comp universe includes eight private peers operating in drones and autonomous verticals, among them Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air; no public comparables exist in this narrowly-defined cohort.

Valuation analysis relies on the stage-progression method, as peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable. The drones and autonomous peer set lacked sufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting quality thresholds—only one adjacent-stage datapoint was identified against a minimum of three required for statistical reliability. The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $16M total raised, treating raised capital as a proxy for post-money valuation at Series A close. This yields an implied valuation of $32M.

The triangulated range supporting the analysis spans $27M (low) to $37M (high), with a median of $32M. This range reflects typical Series A to next-stage progression dynamics. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer benchmarking, which limits validation against sector-specific metrics, and reliance on a stage-based multiplier that may not capture company-specific risk or growth profile. Resolution of these uncertainties would require either access to transaction data from more tightly-filtered peer financing rounds or introduction of revenue or operational metrics for revenue-multiple cross-checks.
